summary.short: EU regulation setting harmonised rules for AI systems and general-purpose AI models in the Union under a risk-based approach: prohibited practices, high-risk requirements, transparency duties, GPAI obligations, sandboxes and EU governance bodies. This extract contains recitals only; operative provisions and application dates are not included.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act) sets out harmonised rules for placing on the market, putting into service and use of AI systems and general-purpose AI models in the Union. It applies to providers established in the Union or in a third country where outputs are used in the Union, and to deployers established in the Union. The recitals describe a risk-based approach. Certain AI practices, including manipulative or exploitative techniques, social scoring, untargeted scraping of facial images, emotion recognition in workplaces and education, and certain law-enforcement biometric uses, should be prohibited. High-risk AI systems in areas such as education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice and elections must meet mandatory requirements on risk management, data governance, documentation, human oversight, accuracy and cybersecurity, and undergo conformity assessment. Transparency duties apply to interaction with AI, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation and deepfakes. Providers of general-purpose AI models have documentation, copyright-policy and training-content summary duties, with further obligations for models presenting systemic risk. The text also refers to an EU database, AI regulatory sandboxes, the AI Office, a Board, a scientific panel and an advisory forum. This extract (part 1 of 3) contains recitals (1) to (153) only; the operative articles, penalties and dates of application are not in the text supplied.

notes: This part (part 1 of 3) contains only the title and the preamble recitals (1 to 152); the heading for recital (153) appears without text. No operative articles are included, so obligations, thresholds, events, definitions and enforcement are annotated in later parts. Relations come from the title (amendments) and preamble (legal basis, cross-references named in recitals); cross-references are limited to instruments named in the recitals. Registry target IDs were not supplied, so target_instrument_id is an empty string for all relations and entities (schema type is string). Entity lei and ticker are empty because they are not in the text. section_status is marked not_applicable only because the schema requires the field; entries are present for both sections. Part 2 of 3 covers recitals 154 to 180 and Articles 1 to 56 (Chapters I to V); Chapter VI onward is in other parts. Recital 156 says Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies in its entirety, but recitals are not coded as relations. Art. 5(3) sets a 24-hour limit for urgent biometric identification authorisation, while Art. 26(10) sets 48 hours for post-remote biometric identification; these are different regimes and are both recorded. Art. 3(48) redirects national authority references for EU institutions to the EDPS. Relation and entity IDs are left empty because registry identifiers were not supplied; references to Annex I, Annex III and Union financial services law are internal or generic and are not coded. Part 3 covers Articles 57 to 113 and Annexes I to XIII. Target_instrument_id is an empty string where the target is not identified in the registry, and lei and ticker are empty strings because none are given in the text. Relations to Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 combine several provisions in one row. Annex X and Annex I list many other acts and are not coded as relations. Internal points: Art. 101(1) contains stray punctuation ('higher., when the Commission finds'); Art. 111(1) refers to Article 113(3), point (a), but Article 113 has no paragraph 3; Art. 113(b) applies the Article 78 and Chapter XII provisions from 2 August 2025 'with the exception of Article 101'. The section_status relations and entities values are schema-required; both sections have entries, so the status shows not_applicable only for conformity.
